summary: M3-S02 (Classic acknowledgement + escalation email templates) tested: xml (4/4 parsed), manifest (consistent), both declared checkers (exit 0), and check-outputs (ok) all passed; 1 manual test (B06) deferred to the M3 milestone gate, tickable from artefacts on disk. Step status set built -> tested.
confidence_rationale: Every declared test ran or was correctly classified as manual; both always-on checks (xml, manifest) completed; every result came from an exit code this agent observed (check_email_templates.py exit 0, check_email_deliverability_strategy.py exit 0, check-outputs exit 0 with ok:true). No checker was missing, no manifest exclusion was needed, and check-outputs reported nothing missing/empty/malformed.

process_observations.observation: Neither template body hardcodes an email address; both are pure merge-field text with no From/Reply-To literal, so the manual test's third observable outcome is satisfied cleanly.
The package.xml is fully consistent in both directions with no wildcard members, so every EmailFolder/EmailTemplate member traces to exactly one file pair and vice versa.

sender-identity-note.md section 2 records an unresolved divergence between plan.json Q22 (support@ itself is the routing address) and answers-key.md's Acknowledgement row (an org-wide address, never the routing address) over whether support@ is safe as the acknowledgement's senderEmail; no test in this step's acceptance_tests[] adjudicates it because EmailTemplate carries no sender element, but the divergence carries forward unresolved into M3-S04 where senderEmail is actually set.

The deliverability checker's three WARNs (no EmailAdministrationSettings/EmailAuthorizationSettings file, no deliverability-policy JSON, no DKIM-key-inventory JSON) are expected given this step declares none of those files, but they mean the checker's exit 0 here carries no assertion at all about deliverability posture -- that gap is intentionally covered by the manual test and the note, not by any exit code in this step.

The Q22-vs-answers-key sender divergence and the inert authorizedSenders control are exactly the kind of finding a deployment-risk or security review would want surfaced before M3-S04 sets senderEmail.
process_observations.followup_reason: because the doc keeper is the next step in this loop and can carry the unresolved Q22 divergence into decisions.md so it is not lost before M3-S04 runs.
